planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Tineke rubber tree holds its cream-and-green variegation best with consistent bright indirect light and needs protection from direct hot sun.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Tineke rubber tree holds its cream-and-green variegation best with consistent bright indirect light and needs protection from direct hot sun. Large, glossy, leathery leaves are marbled in shades of dark green, gray-green, and creamy white with pink-tinged new growth, giving this variegated rubber tree cultivar a soft, marbled color pattern quite different from the solid dark green of the standard species. Grown as a tall, architectural floor plant indoors, it develops into a substantial small tree over years, with new leaves unfurling from a distinctive protective red sheath that drops away as each leaf expands. Wipe dust from the large leaves periodically to keep pores clear, water when the top inch of potting mix dries, and rotate the pot occasionally for even, symmetrical growth.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Ruby rubber tree holds its pink-and-cream variegation best with consistent bright indirect light and needs protection from direct hot sun.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Ruby rubber tree holds its pink-and-cream variegation best with consistent bright indirect light and needs protection from direct hot sun. Large, glossy leaves combine dark green centers with irregular cream margins blushed distinctly pink, the most heavily pink-tinted of the commonly grown variegated rubber tree cultivars, with new growth emerging an even brighter rose-pink from its protective red sheath. Slightly slower growing and somewhat more sensitive to cold and low light than the plain green species or Tineke, it rewards a bright spot with striking color that few other large-leaved floor plants can match. Wipe dust from the leaves periodically, water when the top inch of potting mix dries, and avoid cold drafts, which can cause leaf drop.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; council tree is frost-tender and grown outdoors year-round only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as a large indoor specimen.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; council tree is frost-tender and grown outdoors year-round only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as a large indoor specimen. Broad, rounded, glossy leaves with prominent pale veining and new growth wrapped in a showy pink to red protective sheath make this fast-growing fig a striking large houseplant, and popular variegated selections add irregular cream and yellow margins for even bolder color. In its native range across South and Southeast Asia it grows into a massive banyan-like shade tree valued for the deep shade cast by its broad crown, a scale reflected in the vigor and eventual size it can reach even as an indoor floor specimen if not kept pruned. Wipe dust from the large leaves, water when the top inch of potting mix dries, and prune to control size and encourage a bushier, more branched form.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Song of India is a slow-growing, easy-care dracaena that tolerates lower indoor light better than many variegated foliage plants.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Song of India is a slow-growing, easy-care dracaena that tolerates lower indoor light better than many variegated foliage plants. Narrow, gracefully arching leaves are edged in bright creamy-yellow with a soft green center, densely whorled around slender canes that branch and thicken with age into a full, multi-stemmed small tree, the yellow margins often flushing pink on new growth in bright light. One of the more forgiving variegated dracaenas, it tolerates the lower light and drier air of a typical home or office better than many showier foliage plants, making it a popular, long-lived floor or tabletop specimen depending on its stage of growth. Water when the top inch of potting mix dries, avoid overwatering which causes root rot, and wipe dust from the leaves periodically.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Gold Dust dracaena is one of the more shade-tolerant dracaenas, thriving in dimmer corners better than most foliage houseplants.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Gold Dust dracaena is one of the more shade-tolerant dracaenas, thriving in dimmer corners better than most foliage houseplants. Slender, wiry, bamboo-like canes carry pairs of glossy, dark green, oval leaves speckled with irregular creamy-yellow spots that resemble flecks of gold dust scattered across the foliage, an airy, open growth habit quite different from the dense rosettes of most other dracaenas. Native to West African forest understories, it tolerates lower light than almost any other commonly grown dracaena, making it a good choice for a north-facing window or interior office space with only moderate natural light. Water when the top inch of potting mix dries, avoid overwatering, and prune leggy canes to encourage bushier branching.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Canary Island dragon tree is extremely drought-tolerant once established and tolerates brief light frost but is best suited to zones 9-11 outdoors.

directions: Plant container-grown trees in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Canary Island dragon tree is extremely drought-tolerant once established and tolerates brief light frost but is best suited to zones 9-11 outdoors. Thick, stout, gray trunks branch dichotomously (splitting into two at each growth point) into a distinctive umbrella-shaped crown of stiff, sword-like, blue-green leaves, an ancient, sculptural silhouette that can take a century or more to reach the tree's full mature form. Native to the Canary Islands and named for the dark red resin, called dragon's blood, that oozes from any wound in the bark or trunk, it is exceptionally long-lived, slow-growing, and drought-tolerant once established, making it a striking, low-water architectural specimen for a xeriscape or Mediterranean-style landscape. Water only occasionally once established, avoid overwatering which is the most common cause of failure, and grow young plants in a large container to move under cover during any hard freeze.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Maria Chinese evergreen is exceptionally shade-tolerant and thrives in the low light of interior offices and hallways.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Maria Chinese evergreen is exceptionally shade-tolerant and thrives in the low light of interior offices and hallways. Broad, dark green leaves are marked with irregular silvery-gray feathered patterns radiating from the midrib, a classic, subdued variegation pattern on one of the most durable and widely used interior foliage plants in commercial and office landscaping for its tolerance of low light, dry air, and general neglect. Bred and grown commercially for decades for its reliability in interiorscaping, it is a good starter houseplant for a low-light room where few other flowering or variegated plants would survive. Water when the top inch of potting mix dries, avoid cold drafts below 60°F, and wipe dust from the leaves periodically.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky potting mix; Tricolor Chinese evergreen wants more warmth and humidity than the common commercial aglaonema cultivars and resents cold, drafty conditions.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky potting mix; Tricolor Chinese evergreen wants more warmth and humidity than the common commercial aglaonema cultivars and resents cold, drafty conditions. Deep green leaves are irregularly blotched and speckled in silvery-gray and yellow-green patches in a bold, mottled, camouflage-like pattern that gives this collector-favorite selection its whimsical alternate name, each leaf uniquely patterned in a way that ordinary green or silver aglaonemas never display. Native to forests of Sumatra and Borneo, it is fussier and slower-growing than the ubiquitous commercial aglaonema hybrids, appreciating warmer temperatures, higher humidity, and a chunkier, faster-draining mix than typical potting soil. Water when the top inch of mix dries, avoid temperatures below 60°F, and provide bright indirect light to maintain the bold leaf patterning.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference
